newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Bank of Asia rated sell.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Bank of Asia rated sell.

text.p: Seamico Securities on Thursday rated Thailand's medium-sized Bank of Asia Plc a "sell" based on its rising costs of funds and lack of internal systems development.
Seamico said the bank's heavier than average reliance on foreign funding, at a time when restrictions of foreign credit were being tightened, would increase funding costs.

"As the BOT's (Bank of Thailand's) controls on short-term capital inflows wil remain in place into the foreseesable future BOA will be pressured to increase its portion of local funds and extend the time frame of its foreign borrowings," it said.
"Both these measures will increase the banks funding costs," it added.
Bank of Asia shares were trading steady at 43 baht at 0927 GMT.
Seamico said the bank's loan quality had not deteriorated in line with other Thai commercial banks over the last nine months and that BOA had increased provisioning for doubtful debt to 150 percent.
But it said the large number of bank clients borrowing in foreign currency posed a risk to the bank.

"The BOA has the highest ratio of BIBF (offshore) assets to total assets in the industry (14.6 percent as of September 1996). Although these borrowers are responsible for their own foreign exchange risks the impact will be ultimately felt by BOA if they fail to meet their obligations," it added.
